sections.heading: Why Functional Panic Bars Matter for Arlington Commercial Properties
sections.body: Panic bars — also called push bars or exit devices — are a critical component of commercial door hardware. They allow rapid egress in emergency situations while also serving as a deterrent against unauthorized entry when the door is secured from the outside. In a dense commercial environment like Arlington, where office towers in Rosslyn and mixed-use developments near Pentagon City handle significant daily foot traffic, a malfunctioning exit device is not just an inconvenience — it is a liability. Sticking mechanisms, broken push pads, misaligned latches, and faulty strikes can compromise the safety of everyone in the building. Regular inspection and prompt repair keep exit devices operating smoothly, protecting both occupants and property owners. Our team understands the demands placed on commercial hardware in high-traffic settings and brings the experience needed to restore panic bars to reliable working condition.

sections.heading: Common Panic Bar Problems We Repair in Arlington
sections.body: Exit devices take considerable abuse in busy commercial environments. Over time, components wear, loosen, or break entirely. Our technicians frequently address push rods that have bent or separated from the latch mechanism, making it impossible to open the door from the inside. We also repair broken or cracked push pads, faulty vertical rod assemblies, worn dogging mechanisms that prevent the bar from holding in the unlocked position, and damaged end caps or chassis hardware. Strike plates and door frames often suffer related damage when an exit device is forced or misused, and we assess those components as well. Surface-mounted and concealed vertical rod systems both fall within our scope of work. Whether your building is a glass-front retail space near Ballston Quarter or a multi-story office tower closer to Crystal City, we carry common replacement parts and can source specialized hardware to minimize delays on your repair.

sections.heading: Panic Bar Replacement vs. Repair: What Arlington Buildings Need
sections.body: Not every malfunctioning exit device requires full replacement. In many cases, targeted repair of a specific component — a broken push rod, a worn cam, a misaligned strike — restores full function at a fraction of the cost of replacing the entire unit. Our technicians evaluate each device thoroughly before recommending a course of action. When a panic bar is severely corroded, structurally compromised, or simply at the end of its functional life, replacement is the more cost-effective long-term solution. We help building owners and property managers weigh the options honestly, factoring in the age of the hardware, frequency of use, and overall condition of the door assembly. For glass storefronts and aluminum-framed commercial doors — which are common throughout Arlington's commercial districts — we are experienced with the specific exit devices designed for narrow-stile and wide-stile door systems.
